title: Lean Weekly
description: News about Lean, the theorem prover and programming language.

items.title: Lean becomes first to formalize all 100 theorems on Freek Wiedijk's list
items.content_html:
Freek Wiedijk's page tracking formalizations of 100 theorems, last modified October 29, 2026, shows Lean at 100, with HOL Light and Isabelle next at 95. Kim Morrison reports that the 100th theorem completed in Lean, a strong formulation of Green's theorem (TauCeti.Green.green_ac_index_one), landed in Tau Ceti, a library of AI-authored Lean mathematics.

Sources: kim-em.github.io, cs.ru.nl, taucetiproject.org, leanprover.zulipchat.com

items.title: Mathstodon user markusde posts about porting xv6 to Iris-Lean
items.content_html:
The post includes one attached image and thanks @ahuoguo for noticing the update.

Sources: mathstodon.xyz

items.title: Juan J. Manfredi completes Lean formalization of OpenAI's infinity-harmonic estimates
items.content_html:
The formalization, built on Mathlib, proves the main results of OpenAI's 4 October 2026 preprint, including that infinity-harmonic functions (viscosity solutions of the infinity-Laplace equation) on connected open sets in dimensions 3 and higher are C¹, using only Lean's three standard axioms. Claude agents wrote the Lean proofs with Trellis, an AI-assisted formalization pipeline.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, na0b/infharmonic-lean

items.title: Anthropic publishes Lean formalization of Claude's refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis
items.content_html:
Anthropic's eth/ project, a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, states that a single deterministic Turing machine counts the satisfying assignments of every k-CNF with at least two clauses on at least four variables, each of which occurs, within a step bound that refutes the hypothesis. Claude's paper is in the project folder.

Sources: anthropics/formal-math

items.title: XTX Markets gives £5 million to Imperial College London for Langlands Lab
items.content_html:
The lab for AI-assisted mathematics, led by Kevin Buzzard, will focus on the Langlands program, which seeks connections between fields, particularly number theory and analysis. It aims to produce new results verified in Lean and begins operating in 2027, with the grant supporting five PhD students and three postdoctoral researchers over four years.

Sources: imperial.ac.uk

items.title: Leo de Moura speeds up kernel checking of lia and grind proofs
items.content_html:
Lean's lia (cutsat) now shares proofs across grind case splits, for up to 2.8x faster elaboration and up to 200x faster kernel checking on goals with many case splits. Kernel-friendly certificates for lia, grind's ring solver, simp +arith and grind linarith followed; the ring certificates cut kernel instructions by 51.5% across 40 benchmark files.

Sources: lean4#15905, lean4#15911, lean4#15943, lean4#15981, lean4#15983

items.title: Sebastian Graf merged vcgen +jp, which verifies code after a split once
items.content_html:
Without +jp, vcgen copies the code after an if or a match into every branch, so the number of copies doubles with each consecutive split. With +jp, VC generation grows linearly with the number of splits, and the shared code is verified under a hypothesis stating what each branch knows at its end.

Sources: lean4#14398

items.title: Benjamin Pierce announces Agentic Proof Engineering, a Spring 2027 course at Penn
items.content_html:
The semester course is on building formal proofs about software systems at scale, in collaboration with AI agents, and will also be delivered as a live webinar for participants outside Penn. Some lectures and projects will be phrased in terms of Lean, though fluency with the specifics of Lean will not be needed.

Sources: cis.upenn.edu

items.title: Leo de Moura makes grind failure messages short by default
items.content_html:
Pull request #15906 made diagnostics opt-in via +verbose, so failures showed only the remaining goal and a hint; collecting and printing diagnostics took about 38% of the time spent on easy failing lia goals. Pull request #16073 shortened the failure message further, naming the invoked tactic, such as lia, without printing the goal.

Sources: lean4#15906, lean4#16073

items.title: Mac Malone opens Lake pull request to reduce build-store contention
items.content_html:
The pending change (#15805) has Lake first fetch transitive artifacts from a single build-store snapshot, falling back to the real build store only when an artifact is missing. Mac Malone also opened #16083 to benchmark Lake's module setup computation, which experiments show is a significant scalability chokepoint in projects with thousands of modules.

Sources: lean4#15805, lean4#16083

items.title: GenProof paper on verifying Minecraft redstone circuits uses Lean's bv_decide
items.content_html:
Mike Murunov and Maksim Borisov's gate accepts a redstone layout only with a machine-checkable certificate of equivalence to its Verilog specification. Lean 4 re-proves the claim, unfolding it to one 4-bit equation per node and calling bv_decide, which bit-blasts, runs the CaDiCaL solver and checks its proof with a verified checker.

Sources: paper (pdf)

items.title: Troy Lee formalizes László Babai's graph isomorphism algorithm using an AI agent
items.content_html:
With László Pyber's analysis replacing the classification of finite simple groups, the formalization proves that a single-tape Turing machine (Mathlib's Turing.TM0) decides whether two simple graphs are isomorphic within a quasipolynomial number of transitions. The agent (Claude Code, with Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the Lean code from 18 to 29 October 2026.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, troyjlee/graph-iso-lean

items.title: Adam Gall publishes lean-sudo, a drop-in sudo replacement written in Lean 4
items.content_html:
Its policy, environment and authentication logic is formally verified, with 498 hand-written theorems. On Ubuntu, lean-sudo reads the existing /etc/sudoers, /etc/sudoers.d and /etc/sudo.conf, uses the system's PAM stack, and passes the same 1113-test end-to-end suite as the original sudo, a large C program written around 1980 with a decades-long history of security bugs.

Sources: adamgall/lean-sudo

items.title: holmesworcester publishes Lean Quiet, a chat app written mostly in Lean
items.content_html:
The iOS and Android app uses Lean for everything from TCP packets to pixels; 429 of its 586 theorems are about the code that runs. Because it is local-first, end-to-end encrypted, and peer-to-peer, many properties that would normally depend on a server operator are provable over all possible deployments, assuming user device integrity.

Sources: holmesworcester/lean-quiet

items.title: Scott Armstrong and Zohar Komargodski formalize the positive-measure KAM theorem in Lean
items.content_html:
The headline theorem is proved: for a nearly-integrable Hamiltonian with a small enough perturbation, most of phase space is filled by invariant tori carrying quasi-periodic motion. Agents prove the frozen statements (approved line by line, never edited); 11 of 22 are proved so far, with 73,724 of an estimated 117,000 lines of Lean.

Sources: scottnarmstrong/KAM-dev

items.title: Open-source desktop OS ZENOS releases first preview with Lean-proved security decisions
items.content_html:
ZENOS's services ask zenos-decide, built from the same Lean definitions as the proofs, whether a file opens, content may reach a printer or AI, and a send is allowed, treating missing or unreadable answers as refusals. The theorems rest only on Lean's standard axioms, but the unaudited preview is not for real sensitive data.

Sources: zenos-org/zenos, leanprover.zulipchat.com, zenos v0.1.0-preview

items.title: Anthropic's Claude generates Lean proof of subexponential deterministic factoring
items.content_html:
Isaac Rudich and Louis-Martin Rousseau registered the proof that one deterministic Turing machine computes the smallest prime factor of every natural number N in time N^{o(1)}; the best previously published deterministic bounds known to the authors have exponent 1/5. The authors audited the statement and did not read the proof, which Lean checks.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, IsaacRudich/SubexponentialDeterministicFactoring

items.title: Harmonic's Aristotle proved 185 properties of Tensordyne's most complex block
items.content_html:
Aristotle, an AI that formally verifies software and hardware, also refuted 56 properties of the 12.2 million gate-equivalent block, each with a reproducible counterexample, exposing bugs up to 110,000 cycles after reset. Counting earlier Aristotle runs on sub-blocks, Tensordyne found 8 bugs early in its next chip's design cycle.

Sources: harmonic.fun

items.title: Harmonic's Aristotle fixes three LibTomMath bugs and verifies optimized routines
items.content_html:
Aristotle, Harmonic's AI that formally verifies software, found and repaired three bugs in LibTomMath 1.2.0, which supplies large-integer arithmetic to Tcl and Dropbear SSH. Aristotle then optimized two arithmetic routines, making modular exponentiation 31–38% faster in benchmarks, and proved them against the repaired code's specifications for results, memory safety, errors, and stored values.

Sources: harmonic.fun

items.title: Michael Stoll had Claude build a verified Lean 4 model of ratpoints
items.content_html:
Claude mirrored ratpoints, Michael Stoll's C program that finds rational points on hyperelliptic curves, in Lean function by function and proved, as Comparator certified, that the model meets a short specification. Michael Stoll called the work token-intensive enough to use up a Max 20x subscription's weekly Opus 5.5 allowance within three to four days.

Sources: MichaelStollBayreuth/RatpointsLean, leanprover.zulipchat.com, MichaelStollBayreuth/ratpoints

items.title: Axiom Math formalizes the classification of finite simple groups in Lean
items.content_html:
The complete formalization follows the first-generation proof (thousands of journal pages by about a hundred mathematicians), and Lean's kernel checks every logical step. Axiom Math engineers and mathematicians directed AI agents over 24 days, producing approximately 43.1 million lines of code and finding an issue in a published argument for the Unbalanced Group Theorem.

Sources: axiommath.ai, cfsg.axiommath.ai, AxiomMath/CFSG, hexagonmath.org

items.title: Zhe Ye and coauthors propose agentic verified optimization in Lean 4
items.content_html:
Agents return faster code plus a Lean proof that it equals the original, which serves as the specification. The agents did so for 156 of 189 Verina functions, and 92 proved rewrites sped up 47 of 51 scenarios in 17 applications the authors' Aqueduct framework migrated to Lean from C, C++, Go, or Rust.

Sources: aqueduct.verina.io, arXiv:2610.30188, @0xlf_ on X

items.title: cedar-policy publishes lean-parser-generator, which generates validated LR(1) parsers in Lean
items.content_html:
The tool turns an LR(1) grammar in a .lig file into a compiled Lean parser, plus certificates that Lean checks to prove the parser agrees with a generated dependent specification. It follows the a-posteriori validation architecture also used by Menhir's verified back end, so the automaton construction and code generator need not be trusted.

Sources: cedar-policy/lean-parser-generator

items.title: Software Verification in Lean comes to Stanford University on November 7
items.content_html:
Co-organized by the Beneficial AI Foundation and the Lean FRO, the day of public lectures covers Rust verification with the Aeneas framework, low-level software verification, and formally verified OS kernels. Speakers include Max Tegmark, Shaowei Lin, Leo de Moura, Jonathan Protzenko, Andres Erbsen, and Mike Dodds; a livestream will be available, with recordings afterward.

Sources: @leanprover on X, functional.cafe, bsky.app

items.title: Natalie Marleny announces formal-git, modelling about 30% of Git in Lean 4
items.content_html:
Built over two months with heavy use of coding agents, the project proved more than 8,000 theorems of varying usefulness and uncovered more than 100 potential defects in Git v2.55, including at least two possible security vulnerabilities. Its differential random testing harness and more than 10,000 unique tests will be open-sourced after responsible disclosure.

Sources: @NatalieMarleny on X

items.title: John Zhuoyang Ye and Jens Palsberg verify fault-tolerant quantum compilation in Lean
items.content_html:
The paper introduces QPPM, a language for Pauli-product measurement programs, and verifies lowering of Clifford+T circuits to QPPM and an optimizer that eliminates measurements, fuses and reorders rotations, and schedules logical rounds. On QASMBench, verified fusion and scheduling reduce logical measurement depth by a median of 17.9%.

Sources: arXiv:2610.31694, paperswithlean.com

items.title: Resolution uses Claude Fable 5.1 to formalize Hironaka's resolution of singularities
items.content_html:
The library, written in Lean 4 over Mathlib, proves Hironaka's main theorems in characteristic zero and their refinements by Kollár, Włodarczyk and Bierstone–Milman, for algebraic schemes and analytic manifolds and spaces. Chris Elliott at Resolution directed and audited the automated formalization process, and the code is licensed under Apache License 2.0.

Sources: resolutionorg/hironaka, resolutionorg.github.io, reservoir.lean-lang.org

items.title: Miles Cranmer's AI agents model Julia code in Lean and find bugs
items.content_html:
Lean definitions mirror Julia functions line by line, and each property ends proven, or refuted with a concrete counterexample and a pure-Julia reproducer. In Julia Base and several standard libraries, 400 of 910 properties were refuted and 75 issues filed on JuliaLang/julia; DynamicExpressions.jl, the expression-tree package behind PySR, merged 38 Lean-derived fixes.

Sources: MilesCranmer/julia-in-lean

items.title: Thomas Coratger announces EthLib, a Lean 4 library for Ethereum
items.content_html:
The library, hosted at github.com/ethereum/EthLib, launched with the goal of bringing Ethereum's primitives, specifications and theorems into one place, building a shared foundation for formally specifying and proving things about Ethereum.

Sources: @tcoratger on X

items.title: Katzenpost's Lean library Cryptlib implements the Sphinx cryptographic packet format
items.content_html:
Cryptlib's Sphinx packets are binary compatible with the Katzenpost mix network's Go implementation, including with a post-quantum/classical hybrid key encapsulation method (X25519 and ML-KEM-768) per hop. The AGPLv3-licensed library is for modeling protocols and proving their properties; each kind of primitive has a Lean structure with proposition fields that every instance must satisfy.

Sources: katzenpost/cryptlib, cryptlib.io, reservoir.lean-lang.org

items.title: GitHub user joehattori uses Aeneas and Lean to verify core crosvm components
items.content_html:
In crosvm-verif, Charon and Aeneas extract Rust code and generate Lean, and make verify checks the Lean translation and its specifications. The package is also listed on Reservoir, the package registry for Lake, Lean's build system and package manager.

Sources: joehattori/crosvm-verif, reservoir.lean-lang.org

items.title: Joachim Breitner releases con-agua, a Lean checker with verified x86 assembly
items.content_html:
Written by AI under Joachim Breitner's supervision, con-agua is an x86 assembly port of the external Lean checker con-leche and requires the Kraken x86 semantics to be correct in place of the Lean compiler and runtime. A 5MB assembly file and a 200-line main.c, plus one data file, are all it needs.

Sources: leanprover/con-agua, leanprover.zulipchat.com

items.title: AssureCode uses Lean for structured justification of AI-generated code
items.content_html:
Logan Murphy and coauthors describe AssureCode, which autoformalizes developer intent into Lean specifications for human approval, then decomposes claims via Lean templates, with Lean checking an agent's decomposition-soundness proofs. On HumanEval, LiveCodeBench and MBPP samples with four LLMs, a single run recovered most of an iterative LLM baseline's concerns and surfaced additional ones.

Sources: arXiv:2610.29758, paperswithlean.com

items.title: Wolfram Institute publishes reference Lean environment for Rule 30 Prize submissions
items.content_html:
The verifier checks every submission against exactly this Lake project (Lean 4.35.0, Mathlib's v4.35.0 tag), and the submissions site has instructions for AI agents. The kit contains the official statements of Problems 1 and 2, proved partial results, 163 equivalences and 49 sufficient conditions for Problem 1, and 14 equivalent forms of Problem 2.

Sources: WolframInstitute/Rule30PrizeKit

items.title: Anand Kumar Keshavan announces lean-qverify for verifying quantum circuits in Lean 4
items.content_html:
The open-source project includes a Lean library, a Qiskit integration, and a free workbook with executable examples covering circuit specifications, semantic proofs, Quantum Hoare Logic and ZX-calculus. Anand Kumar Keshavan calls the current implementation an initial research and educational framework, welcomes independent technical reviews, and is interested in collaborating on compositional proof techniques.

Sources: akkeshavan/lean-qverify, leanprover.zulipchat.com, akkeshavan.github.io

items.title: Pranava Kumar registers a Lean proof of Nivat's conjecture with Palomar
items.content_html:
The entry formalizes Pranava Kumar's manuscript, proving that any configuration on the integer plane over a finite alphabet with at most k times n distinct k by n patterns has a nonzero global period. Its independent Challenge states the full conjecture using only standard Mathlib notions; the 339-file proof needs only Lean's foundational axioms.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, PranavaKCode/nivat-lean

items.title: Ziqing Xiang formalizes Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum in Lean
items.content_html:
The Mathlib-based formalization contains the accompanying paper's whole proof that the proportion of n-vertex graphs determined by their generalized spectrum (the spectra of the adjacency matrices of a graph and its complement) tends to 1 as n grows. It also proves the results the paper quotes from the literature, including Kneser's addition theorem.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, ziqingxiang/dgs

items.title: Haruhisa Enomoto formalizes two classical theorems of Bautista, Gabriel, Roiter and Salmerón
items.content_html:
Built on Mathlib, the complete formalization follows Haruhisa Enomoto's new proof that representation-finite algebras over algebraically closed fields have normed multiplicative bases (closed under products up to zero) and basic ones in characteristic other than two are standard (indecomposable modules match their Auslander–Reiten quiver's mesh category). It also proves the Auslander–Reiten theory it uses.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations

items.title: Anirudh Gupta, Siddhartha Gadgil and Petros Markopoulos present PastaLean for verifying Python
items.content_html:
PastaLean deterministically translates Python into Lean through Python's abstract syntax tree, with no LLM, turning specifications written in Python into theorems for agents or humans to prove. It also includes TypeInfer, a Python type inference engine that completed one benchmark in 1.25 s against HeaderGen's 36.2 s, and an MCP server for coding agents.

Sources: anirudhg07.github.io, siddhartha-gadgil/PastaLean, leanprover.zulipchat.com

items.title: Aditya Ranjan Jha and coauthors mechanize a hardware type system in Lean
items.content_html:
Pact, a typed extension of the Anvil hardware description language, checks each component against its type, and compatible types guarantee communication safety (no unsynchronized exchanges or loss of progress). The POPL 2027 paper's artifact includes a Lean 4 mechanization proving soundness of type inference, type checking, and compatibility, plus optimality of inferred types.

Sources: arXiv:2610.26599, doi.org

items.title: Alexander Meiburg disproves perfect randomized composition for total functions, checked in Lean
items.content_html:
Perfect randomized composition (a composition's randomized query complexity is always at least a constant times the product of its factors' complexities) was known to fail for partial Boolean functions but open for total ones. The main result is machine-checked in Lean 4 as a little-o statement on a subsequence of the construction.

Sources: arXiv:2610.31638, paperswithlean.com

items.title: Carlo Ciliberto, Alessandro Rudi, Enrico Tassi introduce Proof-Carrying Contracts for AI agents
items.content_html:
An execution system called the Airlock runs a tool call only if the Lean kernel accepts the agent's proof that the call preserves the agreed constraints in every case its model allows. A Lean 4 mechanization proves the constraints hold at every instant of execution, even for an adversarial agent, under stated assumptions.

Sources: arXiv:2610.28484, consequential-ai/proof-carrying-contracts, paperswithlean.com

items.title: Giulio rebuffo's Janus verifies compiled Go arm64 machine code in Lean 4
items.content_html:
Janus, an early work in progress, decodes instructions in Lean and does not trust the Go compiler, linker, or any source-level reasoning. Every load and store must fall inside a caller-provided allocation, and Go runtime panic stubs (bounds checks, nil, divide) are named outcomes, so "this function never panics" is provable.

Sources: Giulio2002/Janus

items.title: Leo de Moura publishes MiniForth, a Lean tutorial for programming language semantics
items.content_html:
MiniForth's Forth-inspired teaching language, whose programs act on a stack, has arithmetic, DUP, SWAP, DROP, calls, and conditionals. The tutorial embeds it as Lean functions (a shallow embedding) and as data (a deep embedding), proves program equivalences, and adds a second pass where grind handles routine reasoning; the build checks the examples and proofs.

Sources: leodemoura/MiniForth

items.title: ATOMSLab's LeanSMILES formalizes molecular representations and learning algorithms in Lean
items.content_html:
The repository's SMILES toolkit parses SMILES strings into typed molecular graphs, with a canonicity proof for canonical SMILES and an order-invariance proof for RDKit-compatible Morgan fingerprints. Its LeanLearn library covers linear and logistic regression, and the machine-learning pipeline from SMILES to model runs in Lean, with results checked against scikit-learn.

Sources: ATOMSLab/LeanSMILES

items.title: Tanner Duve of Logical Intelligence offers Veil an invariant-synthesis tactic
items.content_html:
Written for Veil, a Lean-based verifier for transition systems, #synthesize_invariants runs the universal PDR algorithm on a module and its safety property. It returns inductive invariants or a counterexample (both proven sound), a "no universal invariant" result (not proven sound) or "unknown"; it succeeded on every Veil example tested within its supported fragment.

Sources: leanprover.zulipchat.com, verse-lab/veil

items.title: Leo de Moura adds three lia changes that avoid large case splits
items.content_html:
The pull requests, merged October 20 and 21, add dynamic variable reordering before large Cooper splits (case splits with as many cases as a variable's coefficient), exact elimination of equations without unit coefficients, and divisibility normalization. Chains of such equations from / and % definitions no longer yield Cooper splits with thousands of cases.

Sources: lean4#15835, lean4#15838, lean4#15827

items.title: Sebastian Ullrich proposes precomputed prefix trees to speed up Lean imports
items.content_html:
The open pull request replaces hash maps of imported constants, built eagerly at import time, with per-module prefix trees precomputed when oleans are written and merged lazily on first access. The change cuts import Lean wall-clock time by 28% and Mathlib's import phase by 21%, in exchange for about 6% larger standard library oleans.

Sources: lean4#14362

items.title: Lean 4 merges libuv buffer fix and refactor from Sofia Rodrigues
items.content_html:
The fix, merged October 14, makes send and recv fail with an invalid-argument error for buffers of 4 GiB or more, instead of letting the length wrap to 32 bits. The refactor, merged October 15, adds owned_ref, a helper that owns Lean objects and helps avoid hundreds of lean_inc and lean_dec in libuv code.

Sources: lean4#15598, lean4#15603

items.title: Thomas Browning and coauthors release AnnalsChallenge, 50 Annals theorems stated in Lean
items.content_html:
Each statement, written by hand in Lean 4 using Mathlib, is the main result of an Annals of Mathematics paper published since 2020; all were manually reviewed, then audited by AI, and are released without formalized proofs. The authors say measuring progress in AI autoformalization of mathematics requires hard, trustworthy datasets of formal statements.

Sources: arXiv:2610.18301
